claim: tinyBenchmarks shows that Item Response Theory, fit on a large cross-model item-correctness matrix, can select a small (~100-item) subset of a benchmark that reliably reproduces full-benchmark rankings, at whole-question granularity.
stance_target: template methodology for principled hard/diagnostic subset mining
scope_conditions: Open LLM Leaderboard, MMLU, HELM, AlpacaEval 2.0; general (non-code) benchmarks
quoted_support: we show that to accurately estimate the performance of an LLM on MMLU, a popular multiple-choice QA benchmark consisting of 14K examples, it is sufficient to evaluate this LLM on 100 curated examples.

claim: tinyBenchmarks' IRT machinery operates on independent whole-benchmark-item responses and has not been applied to code-generation benchmarks with multi-test-case (sub-task/requirement) internal structure.
stance_target: novelty of requirement-level IRT for code benchmarks
scope_conditions: general LLM benchmarks (QA, instruction-following), not code generation
quoted_support: we investigate strategies to reduce the number of evaluations needed to assess the performance of an LLM on several key benchmarks
